headline.title: A software bug slows JPMorgan Chase, and America checks its balance
headline.quip: Chase traced hours of slow transactions to a bug in “on-premise hardware systems,” the three scariest words in banking IT.
headline.summary: Some JPMorgan Chase transactions slowed for hours, with about 4,800 Downdetector reports by 2 p.m. ET; Chase said customers kept access to their accounts and funds. It blamed a “software bug in on-premise hardware systems” and said there was no evidence of a cyber link. Customers of other banks reported problems too; Bank of America, Capital One and U.S. Bank said their own systems weren’t directly affected, and some Zelle payments were delayed.

also.title: United Airlines’ pilot apps stall departures
also.summary: A systemwide outage of more than 90 minutes hit multiple pilot-facing applications at United Airlines, so final aircraft weights couldn’t be provided and departures were delayed. United said there was no sign of a cyberattack.
